Pallet bed calculator

How many Euro pallets do you need for your bed? Enter your mattress size. The calculator shows the best layout, the height, the weight and the cost.

How the calculator works

A Euro pallet measures 1200 × 800 mm and is 144 mm high. The calculator tries both directions, lengthways and crossways to the bed, and picks the layout with the fewest pallets. If the number is the same, the smaller footprint wins. The mattress sits at the head end, and the remaining space stays free at the foot end and the sides as a shelf.

Two layers give a base of 288 mm. With a 20 cm mattress you lie at just under 50 cm, a comfortable sitting height. One layer looks low and relaxed, three layers come close to the height of a normal bed.

Make sure you get Euro pallets (EPAL, 1200 × 800 mm). The standard UK pallet is 1200 × 1000 mm and the Australian standard pallet 1165 × 1165 mm. Neither fits the layouts in this calculator.

Finding the right pallets

Check the stamp on the side: HT means heat treated and is fine indoors. Pallets marked MB were treated with a fumigant and do not belong in a bedroom. Also leave pallets with oil stains, mould or a strong smell where they are.

Used pallets in good condition are often cheap from local suppliers or classified ads, new ones cost more. Adjust the price in the calculator above.

Preparing and assembling

Clean used pallets with a brush and water first and let them dry well for several days. Then sand the top and all visible edges, first with 60 and then 120 grit, so nobody gets splinters. Hardwax oil makes the wood easy to care for and brings out the grain.

Join the pallets in each layer with mending plates and the layers to each other with long wood screws. Furniture glides under the bottom layer protect the floor. A headboard of pallets stood on edge is screwed to the base with brackets and also fixed to the wall.

Bedroom ideas

An LED strip under the top layer makes the bed look as if it floats. The length you need is shown under the result. A border of 20 to 40 cm round the mattress gives you a shelf for books and a lamp, so you can do without a bedside table. Flat baskets fit into the gaps between the blocks. If you want to move the bed often, screw castors with brakes under the bottom layer.

Frequently asked questions

How many pallets do I need for a 140 × 200 or 160 × 200 cm bed?
For both sizes, 4 pallets per layer laid lengthways are enough. That gives a footprint of 160 × 240 cm. With two layers you need 8 Euro pallets, with a headboard 10.
How many pallets do I need for a 180 × 200 cm bed?
Here you need 6 pallets per layer, and the footprint becomes 240 × 240 cm. With two layers you need 12 Euro pallets. A 30 cm shelf stays free on each side.
Do I need slats?
Not necessarily. Air reaches the mattress through the gaps between the deck boards. Sprung and pocket sprung mattresses sit well directly on the pallets. With soft foam mattresses, a simple roll-out slatted base gives more even support. Either way, air the mattress regularly.
How heavy is a pallet bed?
A Euro pallet weighs about 20 to 25 kg. A bed made of 8 pallets therefore weighs around 200 kg. Plan to assemble it in the bedroom and carry the pallets in one at a time.

All timber sections are guide values and do not replace a structural calculation. Carports and patio covers may need planning permission and building regulations approval, and a structural engineer's check depending on where you live.
